title: Equestrian Bowling Arena
description: A physics-based bowling game where the user launches a horse down a lane to knock over an arrangement of ShaderBall pins. The user adjusts launch angle, spin, and power through a multi-step control panel, then watches the rigid-body collision unfold with realistic knockback and scoring.
prompt: Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 that implements an interactive 3D equestrian bowling arena with simulated physics. Load both GLB assets: ShaderBall.glb (used as bowling pins) and horse.glb (used as the bowling projectile). Set up a rectangular bowling lane on a flat ground plane with subtle grid texture. Place 10 ShaderBall instances in a standard triangular bowling pin formation at the far end of the lane, each scaled to roughly 0.4 units and spaced evenly. Place the horse model at the near end facing the pins, scaled appropriately to about 1.2 units tall. Implement a simple rigid-body physics simulation without external libraries: each ShaderBall pin and the horse have position, velocity, mass, and bounding sphere for collision detection. When the horse collides with a pin, apply impulse-based response transferring momentum realistically, and pins can knock into each other via chain collisions. Create a multi-step interaction panel as HTML overlay: Step 1 - a horizontal slider sets launch angle (-15 to +15 degrees). Step 2 - a vertical slider sets launch elevation (0 to 10 degrees). Step 3 - a rotary knob or slider sets sidespin (-5 to +5). Step 4 - a power meter with a moving bar the user clicks to lock power (10 to 100 percent). Step 5 - a Launch button that sends the horse sliding and tumbling down the lane. Step 6 - after the simulation settles (velocities near zero after 4 seconds), display a score overlay counting how many pins were displaced more than 0.3 units from their original position, with a Reset button to replay. Validate each parameter is set before enabling the next step. Use a perspective camera positioned above and behind the horse looking down the lane, with OrbitControls for optional viewing. Add directional light, ambient light, and soft shadows on the ground plane. Animate at 60fps using requestAnimationFrame, stepping physics at fixed 1/60s intervals. The horse should visibly rotate as it travels based on the sidespin value.
